itinerary.summary: Rest is the plan: Leh sits at 3,500 m.

place.name: Rest and hydrate at your hotel
place.description: Flying straight to 3,500 m means your body needs a full day to adjust. Sleep, drink water and skip exertion today; it's what makes the rest of the trip work.

morning.tip: Avoid alcohol for the first 48 hours; ask your doctor about acetazolamide before you fly.

place.name: Leh Main Bazaar stroll
place.description: A gentle walk through the bazaar for apricot jam, pashmina and Ladakhi butter tea, with the Leh Palace above.

afternoon.tip: Walk slowly; the stairs feel steep at this altitude.

place.name: Shanti Stupa sunset
place.description: A white Japanese-built stupa above the town; drive to the top rather than climb the 500 steps on day one.

evening.tip: Take a cab up; save the steps for later in the week.

itinerary.summary: Thiksey, Shey and Hemis along the river.

place.name: Thiksey Monastery morning prayers
place.description: A 12-storey monastery stacked up a hill, often compared to the Potala. Arrive for morning prayers with horns and chanting, then see the two-storey Maitreya Buddha.

morning.tip: Prayers start around 6 AM; arrive quietly and sit at the back.

place.name: Hemis Monastery
place.description: Ladakh's richest monastery, hidden in a side valley, with a fine museum of thangkas and ritual objects.

afternoon.tip: Lunch at the small café by the gate.

place.name: Shey Palace
place.description: The old summer palace of Ladakh's kings, with a giant seated copper Buddha and views over the Indus wetlands.

evening.tip: Back in Leh, apply for your inner-line permits online today for Nubra and Pangong.

itinerary.summary: A high pass, then dunes and a valley of orchards.

place.name: Khardung La pass
place.description: One of the highest motorable passes at about 5,359 m, with prayer flags and views across the Karakoram.

morning.tip: Stop for 15 minutes at most at the top; the altitude is serious.

place.name: Diskit Monastery
place.description: The oldest monastery in Nubra, with a 32-m Maitreya Buddha looking down the valley.

afternoon.tip: Overnight in a Hunder or Diskit camp; Nubra is warmer and lower than Leh.

place.name: Hunder sand dunes
place.description: Cold-desert dunes between the mountains, with double-humped Bactrian camels.

evening.tip: The camel ride is short; the dunes at golden hour are the real show.

itinerary.summary: Through the Shyok valley to the great lake.

place.name: Shyok valley drive
place.description: The direct route along the Shyok river from Nubra to Pangong, through some of Ladakh's wildest scenery.

morning.tip: Road conditions change; your driver will confirm the Shyok route that morning.

place.name: Pangong Tso shore
place.description: The 134-km lake that runs into Tibet, changing from turquoise to deep blue as the light moves.

afternoon.tip: Wind picks up in the afternoon; bring your warmest layer.

place.name: Stargazing at the lake
place.description: With no towns nearby, Pangong's night sky is one of the darkest in India.

evening.tip: Camps run on generators; electricity often stops around 11 PM.

itinerary.summary: A sunrise at the lake and the drive back to Leh.

place.name: Sunrise at Pangong
place.description: The lake at dawn is glassy and silent, the best light of the trip.

morning.tip: Pack the night before so you leave by 9.

place.name: Chang La pass
place.description: Back to Leh over Chang La at about 5,360 m, with a tea stop at the army café on top.

afternoon.tip: Keep water and snacks in the car; there's little on the way.

place.name: Farewell dinner in Leh
place.description: Celebrate with thukpa and skyu (Ladakhi pasta stew) at a garden restaurant in Changspa.

evening.tip: Flights out of Leh leave early; most need you at the airport by 6 AM.

stays.name: The Grand Dragon Ladakh
stays.why: Heated rooms and oxygen on request, reassuring for the first nights at altitude.

stays.name: Stok Palace Heritage
stays.why: Stay in the royal family's palace, 15 km from Leh.

stays.name: Pangong lakeside camps
stays.why: Insulated tents right by the water for the lake night.

essentials.currency: Indian Rupee (INR). UPI and cards work in towns; carry cash for small temples, coracles and rural stalls.
essentials.language: Ladakhi; Hindi and English widely understood
essentials.tipping: Tip your driver about ₹500 a day
essentials.weather: Jun-Sep is the season (Leh 10-25°C, nights near freezing at the lakes).
essentials.gettingAround: Hire a local Ladakh taxi with driver for Nubra and Pangong; outside taxis can't operate between sights. Inner-line permits are applied for online.
essentials.phrase: Julley: hello, thank you and goodbye

packing: Power bank and cash (ATMs are scarce outside Leh)

summary.overview: Five carefully paced days in Ladakh, with a full rest day for acclimatisation built in, monasteries above the Indus, the Nubra valley over Khardung La, and the blue sweep of Pangong Tso.
highlights: Nubra's sand dunes and Diskit monastery
